reviews.review:
A gritty action experience befitting the setting of Warhammer 40,000.

Being a 3rd Person Action experience immediately makes it stand out from the rest of the competition.  With an excellent mix of brutal melee weapons and satisfying guns,  Space Marine excellently pulls-off hack-and-slash gameplay while still being a shooter.

The campaign mode is average, pitting you as an Ultramarines captain fighting against the Ork hordes and the Chaos heretics and Daemons.  The variation is little and overall, the campaign is not truly inspiring.

However, the game shines when it comes to multiplayer.  With basic multiplayer and a wave-based co-op mode, Space Marine breathes much needed life into generic multiplayer modes.

With heavily customizable loadouts and being able to play the roles of Assault, Tactical or Devastator, Space Marine allows players to tailor their loadouts around their playstyle and the needs of the game itself.  With it's unique Dreadnought Assault mode, multiplayer gets hectic while an entire team is faced with a machine capable of wiping them all out.  Space Marine's multiplayer is also blessed with decent lag compensation and speedy host migration (< 10 seconds).

Space Marine brilliantly executes a fusion of Hack-and-Slash and Shooter and brings  this brilliance with it into multiplayer, but unfortunately presents an unispired single player experience.

7/10

Pick it up, if only for the multiplayer.  Worth the $30.

It draws the inevitable comparison to Gears of War, but the folks at Relic did a nice job of making this one feel like it's own game, not some cash-in clone.  The world of Warhammer 40k is nicely realized and the action is often great (shoot orcs from afar with your huge gun, close distance and hack and slash the horde to peices with your chainsword, rinse-and-repeat).  Charaters are a bit flat but the story is interesting and well-paced.  B+

There's a lot of great things going on for this title. Beautiful graphics, good voice acting and visceral intense combat. But for everything right there is something wrong. While the graphics are nice there is a real lack of variety in the level design. I know it's mostly because of the universe but the color scheme is drab and levels are linear. The weapons mostly feel very underpowered and my lord this game is repetitive. If you want to kill orks, this is mana from heaven but that is literally ALL you do. Kill orks, hit switches rinse and repeat. Another gripe, I just killed 2500+ enemies through the course of the game and I'm rewarded with a terribly unsatisfying ending.  Do I still recommend this title? Yes but only mildly.  Because of the constant checkpoint saves you can jump in, kill some orks and get out so there's that.  One last thing, do NOT get the DLC unless you plan on playing MP.  It won't do you any good in the SP campaign.
